name: Permafrost and permafrost thaw – the North

geo.extent: Territories, northern parts of the provinces, high Cordillera

description: About one-half of Canada's land surface is underlain by permafrost: continuous in the north (about 100 m thick at its southern limit to 1,000 m in the Far North) and discontinuous to the south. Thawing permafrost is among the effects of warming already evident in Canada, and northern Canada has warmed at more than double the global rate (CCCR 2019). Thaw damages foundations, roads and airstrips.

practical_implications: Specialised foundations (piles) and higher construction and maintenance costs
Seasonal road access (winter roads) is shortening
